newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end mixed in last-minute rally.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end mixed in last-minute rally.

text.p: Dutch shares closed mixed on Thursday, dragging themselves up from the day's lows in a last-hour rally as Wall Street extended Wednesday's 96 point gain with another rise at its opening.
The AEX share index closed 0.83 points easier at 588.60, up from an earlier session low of 586.48.

But dealers said investors mistrusted the trend on Wall Street and were happier to take their cue from markets closer to home such as London and Frankfurt, which showed solid declines. "It's not normal when Wall Street is up 100 points and we're down, you don't see that happening too often," said a trader.
Dealers had expected Dutch shares would rise initially on the back of Wall Street's surge overnight to another record high, boosted by Bill Clinton's re-election as U.S. president.

Instead the AEX fell and, after a brief foray higher, was down for most the day. "There are some expectations that the rally on Wall Street won't go on for much longer and investors remain cautious about the interest rate outlook," a dealer said.

Dealers said investors had had their appetite for stock blunted by the recent run of flat or disappointing company earnings announcements, including third quarter trading figures from chemicals firm Akzo on Wednesday.

Dealers said Thursday's last minute share rally was accompanied by a modest bond market recovery, which if it and the Wall Street gain held out, could pave the way for Dutch shares to gain ground on Friday.
"Maybe we can expect a rise tomorrow, but there's still a lot of caution about third quarter figures which have been a little disappointing recently," a trader said.

Others took a different view, predicting further churning between 585 and 590 on the AEX. "There's plenty of cash around but it's not a bullish market at the moment and it means we will continue to consolidate at these levels," said another dealer.
